related_questions.question: Which COVID are we on now?
related_questions.snippet: What COVID-19 variant are we on? Currently, the dominant variant nationwide is LP.8.1, with 38% of cases, followed by NB.1.8.1, with 37% of cases, and XFG, with 8% of cases. "The original omicron variant is gone now," says Dr. Rupp.

related_questions.question: How long after I am exposed to COVID will I get it?
related_questions.snippet: Symptoms may appear 2-14 days after exposure to the virus. Symptoms may start as mild, and some people will progress to more severe symptoms.
related_questions.title: Symptoms of COVID-19 - CDC

related_questions.question: How do people get COVID-19 now?
related_questions.snippet: When someone with COVID-19 breathes, speaks, coughs or sneezes, they release small droplets containing the virus. You can catch it by breathing in these droplets, or by touching surfaces covered in them and then touching your eyes, nose or mouth. You are more likely to catch it indoors and in crowded places.
related_questions.title: How to avoid catching and spreading COVID-19 infection. - NHS

related_questions.question: What is the quickest time to get rid of COVID?
related_questions.snippet: The average recovery time for those who have mild or normal cases of COVID-19 or flu is between one and two weeks. If you have COVID-19, the CDC recommends isolation from others until your symptoms are getting better and you are fever-free for 24 hours without the use of fever-reducing medication.
